Maria R.: heads up — ran into a weird case in billing where a request falls back from prod-llama-v2 to small-v1 and we double-charge the token. any quick ideas?
Sam K.: ugh. double-charge meaning both models emit tokens and we attribute all of them?
Maria R.: yeah, client asked for prod-llama, runtime routed -> small-v1. we record usage at the serving side and again at the fallback. looks like two events with different model ids and same request_id.
Alex T.: is the request_id the canonical one across the routing layer? or are we generating a new one per model hop?
Maria R.: router preserves request_id but downstream producers stamp their own event_id. current billing join keys are (request_id, model_id) so it splits.
Jamal P.: quick thought: attach an "origin_model" marker and only charge for the first successful model in the chain. fallback events become metadata-only.
Sam K.: that presumes we can reliably decide "first successful" at ingest time. what about retries where first attempt timed out but produced partial tokens later?
Alex T.: we could add a finalization step — finalizer service consumes model events, orders by event_ts, and emits a single canonical charge event with the chosen model_id and token_count. originals become audit records but not billed.
Maria R.: that sounds right. tradeoffs: adds latency to billing visibility and needs strong ordering guarantees.
Jamal P.: ordering: we have ingest partitioned by request_id shard. finalizer can use a watermark window (e.g., 30s) then finalize. late arrivals require correction path.
Sam K.: 30s might be fine for most, but ops will get nervous about delayed billing dashboards. can we emit provisional metrics and then adjust?
Alex T.: provisional events + reconciliation is standard. emit a provisional charge with a provisional flag; finalizer emits an "adjustment" if needed. dashboards should be wired to show provisional vs finalized.
Maria R.: ok. question: how to ensure audits show both the fallback trace and final billing choice? compliance needs both.
Jamal P.: keep both: ingest raw events into cold store (s3) and keep the finalized charge in the fast ledger. Link via request_id and canonical_charge_id. Auditors can join on those ids.
Sam K.: sounds good. but storage costs rise if we keep full raw payloads. maybe strip large logits/embeddings before archiving.
Maria R.: agreed. redact heavy payloads before cold-store. we only need metadata + small context for audits.
ops-oncall: infra-bot detected an increased fanout on the metering topic at 15:43; routing fanout limiter engaged (check #eng-infra). FYI :rotating_light:
infra-bot: deploy:finalizer-service v2.3 rolled to canary in us-west-2 at 15:46 — monitors_online: true
Alex T.: another edge: what if fallback model is cheaper but generates more tokens (worse rate). finalizer must pick the economically correct charge. do we charge by requested model or actual model used?
Maria R.: product says charge for actual model used. customers care about what they consumed. but we need transparency: show both requested_model and executed_model in billing breakdown.
Jamal P.: final plan proposal: 1) ingest raw model events keyed by request_id 2) emit provisional charges at ingest for near-real-time dashboards (tagged provisional) 3) run finalizer windowed by request_id (30s) to choose canonical executed_model and produce finalized charge 4) finalizer emits adjustments if provisional != final 5) raw events archived (redacted) for audits, linked to final charge via canonical_charge_id
Sam K.: + add a small SLA for finalization window and a manual escalation playbook for long-tails.
Maria R.: sounds actionable. I'll draft a short RFC with schema changes: add canonical_charge_id, provisional boolean, origin_model_id, requested_model_id, and a redaction flag. cc @Alex T. @Jamal P.
Alex T.: thanks. also include a sample event JSON for the canonical_charge and adjustment flows.
Maria R.: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
ops-oncall: noted — if finalizer increases consumer lag we'll throttle provisional emit to protect the metering topic.
